title: Tensor-action and open-counit identities for finite-level projection maps
statement:
Use the finite coefficient ring $A=A_{E,n}$, $n\geq1$, and field $k$ of [def-pur-conventions]. All schemes are separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Work in their ambient small pro-etale derived categories with pullback and tensor [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]; write $P_u=Lu^*$, $R_u=Ru_*$ and $\otimes=\otimes_A^L$, and use the canonical tensor associators and the pullback/tensor comparisons $\mu_{u;N_1,N_2}:P_u(N_1\otimes N_2)\xrightarrow{\sim}P_uN_1\otimes P_uN_2$.

1. *Proper maps.* Let $u:V\to W$ be proper [def-weil-proper-morphism] and let $\pi_{u;M,N}:R_uM\otimes N\to R_u(M\otimes P_uN)$ be precisely the counit-defined projection map [def-exchange-projection]. For arbitrary $M\in D(V_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ and $N_1,N_2\in D(W_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$, under the associators and $\mu_u$,
$$\pi_{u;M,N_1\otimes N_2}=\pi_{u;M\otimes P_uN_1,N_2}\circ(\pi_{u;M,N_1}\otimes1_{N_2}).$$
2. *Open immersions.* Let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion], with exact extension by zero $j_!\dashv j^{-1}$, counit $\varepsilon_j:j_!j^{-1}\to1$, and canonical tensor isomorphism $\delta_{j;M,N}:j_!M\otimes N\xrightarrow{\sim}j_!(M\otimes j^{-1}N)$ of [lem-cbc-extension-zero-projection-formula]. For arbitrary $M$ on $U$ and $N_1,N_2$ on $X$, under the associators and $\mu_j$,
$$\delta_{j;M,N_1\otimes N_2}=\delta_{j;M\otimes j^{-1}N_1,N_2}\circ(\delta_{j;M,N_1}\otimes1_{N_2}).$$
For arbitrary $F,N$ on $X$, as maps $j_!j^{-1}F\otimes N\to F\otimes N$,
$$\varepsilon_{j,F\otimes N}\circ j_!(\mu_{j;F,N}^{-1})\circ\delta_{j;j^{-1}F,N}=\varepsilon_{j,F}\otimes1_N.$$
3. *Compactifications.* For a separated finite-type morphism $f:X\to Y$ with a chosen compactification $c=(j,p)$, the compactification projection map $\operatorname{PF}^c_{f;M,N}:Rp_*j_!M\otimes N\to Rp_*j_!(M\otimes Lf^*N)$ of [def-exchange-projection] satisfies the tensor-action identity of clause 1, with $Rp_*j_!$ in place of $R_u$ and $Lf^*$ in place of $P_u$.

These are identities of the actual maps, before imposing invertibility on any projection map. The same assertions hold on the ordinary etale derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], using exact inverse image, ordinary derived tensor [def-kun-derived-tensor], the same counit-defined proper projection maps and open tensor isomorphisms, and the compactified compact-support functors $Rp_*j_!$ of [def-amb-etale-compact-support, lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons].

proof.text: Fix the canonical associators. On the pro-etale categories, the finite-level clause of [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso] gives natural tensor comparisons compatible with associators and with composition of pullbacks. On the ordinary etale categories use [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] for the morphism of ringed topoi induced by $u$ with constant ring $A$; its isomorphism is the inverse of the canonical comparison of [lem-kun-inverse-image-monoidal], which is the one entering [def-kun-projection-formula-map] and [lem-kun-derived-pullback-composition-monoidal] (both are the Stacks 07A4 comparison for that morphism of ringed topoi). This canonical comparison has the same associativity normalization: on K-flat representatives with flat terms both iterated comparisons send $s\otimes((x\otimes y)\otimes z)$ to $((s\otimes x)\otimes(1\otimes y))\otimes(1\otimes z)$ after reassociation. The associators are induced by reassociation on total tensors by [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal]; the two paths preserve the degrees and have no permutation signs. The K-flat localization equivalence in [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] makes equality on these representatives equality in the derived category, in three variables by applying the equivalence in each variable. We may therefore write $P(A\otimes B\otimes C)=PA\otimes PB\otimes PC$ in the following calculations, always using these fixed comparisons.

Write $P=Lu^*$, $R=Ru_*$ and $e:PR\to1$ for the direct-image adjunction counit. By [def-exchange-projection], $\pi_{M,N}$ is the transpose of $(e_M\otimes1)\mu_{RM,N}$. For the ordinary etale categories this is precisely the definition in [def-kun-projection-formula-map]. The natural adjunction bijection and its inverse formula of [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection] give, under the comparisons of Step 1,
$$e_{M\otimes PN}\,P\pi_{M,N}=e_M\otimes1_{PN}.$$
Indeed, the transpose of $R(a)\eta$ is $e\,PR(a)P\eta=a\,eP\eta=a$, by counit naturality and the triangle identity. Equality of the transposes detects equality of the original arrows.

Put $M_1=M\otimes PN_1$ and $M_{12}=M_1\otimes PN_2$. Transpose the iterated projection map under $P\dashv R$. Naturality of $\mu$ and Step 2 give
$$\begin{aligned}
e_{M_{12}}P\bigl(\pi_{M_1,N_2}(\pi_{M,N_1}\otimes1)\bigr)
&=(e_{M_1}\otimes1)(P\pi_{M,N_1}\otimes1)\\
&=(e_{M_1}P\pi_{M,N_1})\otimes1\\
&=e_M\otimes1_{PN_1}\otimes1_{PN_2}.
\end{aligned}$$
The single map $\pi_{M,N_1\otimes N_2}$ has exactly this transpose, after $P(N_1\otimes N_2)\cong PN_1\otimes PN_2$ and reassociation. The bijection in [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection] proves clause 1 on both sites. Properness is permitted but was not needed; in particular no invertibility of $\pi$ entered.

For the open immersion write $J=j_!$, $Q=j^{-1}$ and $v:1\to QJ$ for the open adjunction unit. On the pro-etale site, [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization] identifies the inverse $\kappa_{M,N}=\delta_{M,N}^{-1}$ of the exact canonical open tensor map of the statement: its transpose is
$$b_{M,N}=\mu_{j;JM,N}^{-1}(v_M\otimes1):M\otimes QN\longrightarrow Q(JM\otimes N).$$
This is an assertion about the specified open tensor map, not a choice of some isomorphism between its endpoints. In particular
$$Q\kappa_{M,N}\,v_{M\otimes QN}=b_{M,N}.$$
We use the adjunction bijection of [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection] for $J\dashv Q$ when comparing open maps below.

source.place: Tag 0GL1 and sites-modules.tex Tag 0E8I: open-unit normalization

proof.text: The same normalization holds for the ordinary etale map of [lem-pur-etale-open-derived-tensor]. To check it without identifying the two sites, take its defining sheaf tensor comparison on the localized etale site. Its inverse takes $j_!(m\otimes qn)$ to $j_!m\otimes n$ on objects over the open. Under the sheaf adjunction of [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction] this is $v_M\otimes1$ followed by inverse restriction/tensor comparison: the counit there is induced by the identity on sections over the open. These statements are equalities of sheaf maps, determined by the zero-extension presheaf and sheafification, not a test on cohomology stalks. Represent $N$ by a K-flat complex with flat terms. Pullback of that representative is K-flat by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], and the definition of the derived comparison in [lem-pur-etale-open-derived-tensor] is the direct-sum totalization of just these sheaf maps. Consequently the same formula for $b$ and $\kappa$ holds for arbitrary unbounded $M,N$. Exact extension by zero [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact] and exact inverse image mean their units and counits are the degreewise ones. Thus Steps 4, 6 and 7 apply separately on each site with its own adjunction.

proof.text:
Set $M_1=M\otimes QN_1$ and $M_{12}=M_1\otimes QN_2$. Compare $\kappa_{M,N_1\otimes N_2}$ with
$$h=(\kappa_{M,N_1}\otimes1)\kappa_{M_1,N_2}:JM_{12}\longrightarrow JM\otimes N_1\otimes N_2.$$
Its transpose, using the open units and the comparisons of Step 1, is
$$Qh\,v_{M_{12}}
=(Q\kappa_{M,N_1}\otimes1)(v_{M_1}\otimes1)
=v_M\otimes1_{QN_1}\otimes1_{QN_2}.$$
This is also the transpose of the single $\kappa_{M,N_1\otimes N_2}$. Injectivity of the adjunction bijection [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection] gives equality. Inverting this equality yields exactly the open tensor-action identity for $\delta$ in clause 2, with its displayed order of factors.

source.place: Tags 0GL1 and 0E8I: explicit inverse-open-map tensor calculation

proof.text:
Let $e:JQ\to1$ now be the open counit and put $D=F\otimes N$. Cancel the isomorphism $\delta_{QF,N}$ on the right in the desired counit equation. It is enough to show
$$e_DJ(\mu_{j;F,N}^{-1})=(e_F\otimes1)\kappa_{QF,N}:
J(QF\otimes QN)\longrightarrow D.$$
The transpose of the left side is $\mu_{j;F,N}^{-1}$, by naturality of the open unit and $Qe_Dv_{QD}=1$. By Steps 4--5 the transpose of the right side, after the tensor comparison, is
$$\mu_{j;F,N}^{-1}(Qe_F\otimes1)(v_{QF}\otimes1)
=\mu_{j;F,N}^{-1},$$
using $Qe_Fv_{QF}=1$. The adjunction bijection and its triangle identities [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection] give equality. Recompose with $\delta_{QF,N}$ to obtain the exact counit equation of clause 2. This checks the actual counits, including on arbitrary unbounded complexes.

source.place: Tags 0E8I and 0GL1: counit compatibility by the open triangle identity

proof.text:
Fix $c=(j,p)$ and write $R=Rp_*$, $P=Lp^*$, $J=j_!$, $Q=Lj^*$. The definition [def-exchange-projection] is $\mathrm{PF}_{M,N}=R(\delta_{M,PN})\pi_{JM,N}$, followed by $QP=Lf^*$. To expand two successive factors, put $M_1=M\otimes QPN_1$ and $A=JM$. Naturality of the counit-defined $\pi$ in its first variable moves $R(\delta_{M,PN_1})$ across $\pi_{JM_1,N_2}$, so that
$$\begin{aligned}
\mathrm{PF}_{M_1,N_2}(\mathrm{PF}_{M,N_1}\otimes1)
&=R\bigl(\delta_{M_1,PN_2}(\delta_{M,PN_1}\otimes1)\bigr)
\pi_{A\otimes PN_1,N_2}(\pi_{A,N_1}\otimes1)\\
&=R(\delta_{M,P(N_1\otimes N_2)})\pi_{A,N_1\otimes N_2}\\
&=\mathrm{PF}_{M,N_1\otimes N_2}.
\end{aligned}$$
The second equality is Step 6 for $PN_1,PN_2$ and Step 3 for $p$; Step 1 supplies the tensor comparisons. For $QP=Lf^*$ the pro-etale composition/tensor normalization is [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso], and the ordinary etale one is [lem-kun-derived-pullback-composition-monoidal]. On the ordinary etale categories use exactly the composite $Rp_*j_!$ of [def-amb-etale-compact-support]; the same expansion defines its compactification projection map, using [def-kun-projection-formula-map] and Step 5. No compactification-independent exchange or comparison is used. This proves clause 3 on both sites.
